beats.text: A model only produces text. So how does it act?
beats.say: A language model can only produce text. So how does an agent actually do things?

beats.text: Step 1: describe each tool to the model.
beats.say: First, you describe each tool to the model: its name, what it does, and its parameters.

beats.text: Step 2: the model asks. It never runs the tool.
beats.say: When the model decides a tool is needed, it doesn't run it. It outputs a structured request: the tool name, and the arguments.

beats.text: Step 3: your code runs it and returns the result.
beats.say: Your code runs the tool, and sends the result back to the model as a new message.

beats.text: Step 4: the model uses the result.
beats.say: The model then uses that result to write its final answer, or to decide on another tool call.

beats.text: Good tools: clear names, precise docs, validated args.
beats.say: Good tool design matters: clear names, precise descriptions, and validated arguments. The model can only be as careful as the tools you give it.

beats.text: Next up: the ReAct loop. Follow for more!
beats.say: Next up, the ReAct loop. Follow for more agentic AI.
